questions.statement: Choose the correct collocation: 'She decided to ____ the offer.'

options.feedback: 'Refuse an offer' is possible but changes the meaning; the neutral verb is 'accept'.
'Make an offer' is the collocation used from the side of the person who offers.
'Accept an offer' is a fixed and natural collocation.
'Take an offer' is not a standard English collocation.

questions.explanation:
'Accept an offer' es una combinacion fija y natural del ingles; las demas no encajan con 'offer' en este sentido.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which adjective and noun form a natural collocation?

options.feedback: 'Close enemy' is not idiomatic; one says 'a sworn enemy'.
'Close friend' is a fixed combination in English.
'Immediate' describes time or sequence, not friendship.
'Near' refers to distance or time, not to closeness of a bond.

questions.explanation:
'Close friend' es una combinacion fija del ingles; 'close enemy' no lo es: se dice 'bitter enemy' o 'sworn enemy'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'The teacher asked the students to ____ their homework carefully.'
questions.context: Verbo y sustantivo en collocations, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'Make' collocates with a meal or a decision, not with homework in this sense.
'Write' takes 'an essay' or 'a report', not 'homework'.
'Take' collocates with an exam or a medicine, not with homework.
'Do homework' is the standard verb-noun collocation.

questions.explanation:
'Do one's homework' es la collocation estandar; los demas verbos no se combinan de forma natural con 'homework'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the best verb: 'We need to ____ a decision before Friday.'

options.feedback: 'Do' collocates with tasks, homework or business, not with a decision.
'Make a decision' is the fixed collocation in standard English.
'Take a decision' appears in some legal registers but is not the common collocation.
'Give a decision' would suggest handing the decision over to someone else.

questions.explanation:
'Make a decision' es la combinacion natural del ingles; 'do a decision' no existe.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which prepositional collocation is correct?

options.text: She is responsible of the project.
options.feedback: 'Responsible of' is not standard English; use 'for'.

options.text: She is responsible from the project.
options.feedback: 'From' would suggest origin, not responsibility.

options.text: She is responsible to the project.
options.feedback: 'Responsible to' takes a person, not a task.

options.text: She is responsible for the project.
options.feedback: 'Responsible for' is the fixed prepositional collocation.

questions.explanation:
En ingles se dice 'responsible for'; las demas preposiciones no forman parte de esa collocation.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the natural collocation: 'He is very ____ about arriving on time.'

options.feedback: 'Concerned about' is the natural collocation with punctuality.
'Concerning' is a preposition meaning 'about' and cannot follow 'very'.
'Concern' is a noun here and cannot follow 'very' in this pattern.
'Concernful' is not a standard English adjective.

questions.explanation:
La combinacion fija es 'concerned about', que expresa preocupacion o interes. Expresa worried about, pleased with o surprised at.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'The weather was so ____ that the match was cancelled.'
questions.context: Collocations con el clima, San Miguel.

options.feedback: 'Strong rain' is not idiomatic; one says 'heavy rain' or 'torrential rain'.
'Heavy rain' is the standard English collocation.
'Hard rain' is informal and refers to droplets, not to intensity here.
'Big rain' is informal and does not fit a formal register.

questions.explanation:
'Heavy rain' es la combinacion natural del ingles; 'strong rain' no se usa. El adjetivo describe la intensidad de la precipitacion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which verb goes with the noun 'progress'?
questions.context: Collocaciones con sustantivos abstractos, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'Do' does not collocate with 'progress' in standard English.
'Take' collocates with a bath, a break or a decision.
'Make progress' is the fixed and standard combination.
'Get' would require an adjective: 'get progress' is not idiomatic.

questions.explanation:
'Make progress' es la collocation estandar del ingles; 'do progress' no existe. Tambien se dice 'make headway' con el mismo sentido.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the best adjective for the noun 'rain': 'We had ____ rain this year, so the reservoir is full.'

options.feedback: 'Abundant rain' is a natural collocation meaning plentiful rain.
'Abundante' is not a standard English adjective.
An adverb cannot modify the noun 'rain' in this position.
'Abundancy' is a noun and does not modify 'rain'.

questions.explanation:
'Abundant rain' describe una cantidad grande de lluvia y combina natural con 'rain'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'We are looking forward to ____ the festival next month.'
questions.context: Collocaciones con 'look forward to', San Salvador.

options.feedback: The base form is wrong after the preposition-like 'to' in 'look forward to'.
A noun would need no 'to' before it: 'look forward to the celebration'.
'Celebrated' is a past participle and cannot follow 'to' here.
'Look forward to' is always followed by a gerund or a noun.

questions.explanation:
Despues de 'look forward to' se usa un gerundio o un sustantivo; por eso corresponde 'celebrating'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which phrase is the correct collocation?

options.text: She makes a research on climate change.
options.feedback: 'Make a research' is not idiomatic; one says 'do research'.

options.text: She does a research about climate change.
options.feedback: 'A research' is not standard; 'research' is uncountable in this sense.

options.text: She carries out research on climate change.
options.feedback: 'Carry out research' is a standard collocation and 'research' is uncountable here.

options.text: She makes researches on climate change.
options.feedback: 'Researches' as a countable plural is rare and 'make' is not its verb.

questions.explanation:
'Carry out research' es una collocation estandar y 'research' funciona aqui como sustantivo incontable.

questions.statement: Complete: 'The doctor recommended me to ____ more exercise.'
questions.context: Collocaciones con verbos de recomendacion, San Miguel.

options.feedback: 'Make exercise' is not a natural collocation in English.
'Give exercise' is not idiomatic in English.
'Take exercise' exists in British English but 'recommend me to take' is less natural than 'do'.
'Recommend somebody to do' is a standard recommendation pattern.

questions.explanation:
El patron estandar es 'recommend somebody to do something' o 'recommend doing something'.

questions.statement: Choose the correct verb-noun collocation.
questions.context: Collocaciones de verbos y sustantivos, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'Pay attention' is a fixed collocation in English.
'Do attention' does not exist in English.
'Make attention' is not idiomatic.
'Give attention to' takes a problem as its object, not the act of listening.

questions.explanation:
'Pay attention' es una collocation fija; el verbo 'pay' se combina con 'attention', 'a bill' y 'a price'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the natural collocation with the adjective 'strong'?

options.feedback: 'Strong water' is not a standard collocation.
'Strong rain' is not idiomatic; one says 'heavy rain'.
'Strong food' is not a standard collocation in everyday English.
'Strong coffee' is a natural collocation describing a high caffeine content.

questions.explanation:
'Strong coffee', 'strong tea' y 'strong opinion' son combinaciones naturales; 'strong water' no lo es.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She has a ____ for classical music.'

options.feedback: 'Have a passion for' is a fixed collocation meaning a strong love for something.
'Passion to' is not correct; the preposition is 'for'.
'Of' would need a following noun: 'a passion of music' is wrong.
'At' does not introduce the object of this collocation.

questions.explanation:
'Have a passion for' es una collocation natural; la preposicion debe ser 'for'. 'She has an affinity for art' funciona con el mismo sentido.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the natural expression: 'The story is so ____ that I could not stop reading it.'

options.feedback: 'Excited' describes the reader's feeling, not the quality of the story.
'Excitement' is a noun and cannot complete 'is so' without an adjective.
The story causes the excitement, so the adjective describing it is 'exciting'.
'Excitedly' is an adverb and cannot follow the linking verb 'is'.

questions.explanation:
'Exciting' describe lo que provoca emocion; 'excited' describe la emocion de la persona.

questions.statement: Which of these verb and particle combinations does not exist in English?

options.feedback: 'Turn down' is a real phrasal verb meaning to lower the volume or refuse.
'Spend off' is not an English verb-particle combination.
'Give up' is a real phrasal verb meaning to stop trying.
'Look after' is a real phrasal verb meaning to take care of.

questions.explanation:
'Turn down', 'give up' y 'look after' son phrasal verbs reales; 'spend off' no existe.

questions.statement: Complete: 'The company had to ____ its production because of the strike.'
questions.context: Collocaciones de verbos de negocio, San Salvador.

options.feedback: 'Cut back on' is a natural collocation meaning to reduce the amount.
'Cut off' means to interrupt a relationship or a supply, not to reduce production.
'Cut down' normally collocates with trees.
'Cut away' describes removing material from a surface.

questions.explanation:
'Cut back on' significa reducir la cantidad y es la combinacion natural con 'production'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses natural collocations throughout?
questions.context: Revision final de collocations, San Salvador.

options.text: The committee will do a decision, get an agreement and arrive the deadline.
options.feedback: None of these three combinations is idiomatic in standard English.

options.text: The committee will take a decision, reach an agreement and meet the deadline.
options.feedback: All three verb-noun pairs are standard English collocations.

options.text: The committee will make a decision, achieve an agreement and touch the deadline.
options.feedback: 'Make a decision' is correct, but the other two pairs are not natural.

options.text: The committee will take a decision, reach an agreement and hit the deadline.
options.feedback: 'Hit the deadline' exists informally, but 'meet the deadline' is the standard formal collocation.

questions.explanation:
'Take a decision', 'reach an agreement' y 'meet a deadline' son las tres collocaciones estandar de la oracion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct adverb: 'She completed the task ____.'

options.feedback: 'In time' means soon enough to be able to do something, not exactly by the deadline.
'At time' requires a specific hour and is not idiomatic on its own.
'On time' is the fixed collocation for meeting a deadline.
'With time' means 'as time passes' and does not express punctuality.

questions.explanation:
'On time' es la expresion fija para indicar que algo se hizo dentro del plazo. 'In time' se reserva para llegar con margen suficiente.
